A 30-year-old woman (G2P2) experiences ongoing vaginal bleeding immediately following vaginal
delivery. Her labor was induced over 30 hours using continuous oxytocin infusion. The pregnancy had
been uncomplicated, and her only medication is albuterol for asthma. Following delivery of an intact
placenta, cumulative blood loss surpasses 1050 mL. Despite aggressive management including uterine
massage, intramuscular oxytocin, and continued oxytocin infusion, the uterus remains boggy.
Examination reveals no cervical lacerations or clots in the lower uterine segment. What is the most
appropriate next intervention for this patient? Answer Choices: (A) Perform manual exploration of
uterus (B) Administer methylergonovine intramuscularly (C) Initiate crystalloid fluid resuscitation (D)
Initiate tranexamic acid infusion (E) Provide an additional dose of oxytocin intravenously (F) Begin
misoprostol administration (G) Administer carboprost intramuscularly (H) Perform immediate
hysterectomy (I) Insert Bakri balloon (J) Begin fresh frozen plasma transfusion
 A. Begin fresh frozen plasma transfusion
B. Provide an additional dose of oxytocin intravenously
C. Perform manual exploration of uterus
D. Administer carboprost intramuscularly
E. Initiate crystalloid fluid resuscitation
F. Begin misoprostol administration
G. Administer methylergonovine intramuscularly
H. Initiate tranexamic acid infusion
I. Insert Bakri balloon
J. Perform immediate hysterectomy
